artworks.title: Hecuba and Polyxena
artworks.description: Oil painting by the French Neoclassicist Merry-Joseph Blondel, now in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art. After the fall of Troy, the aged queen throws a protective arm around her daughter Polyxena, whom the Greeks claimed for sacrifice at the tomb of Achilles.

artworks.title: Hecuba Blinds Polymestor
artworks.description: Oil painting by the Bolognese painter Giuseppe Maria Crespi, in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels. Hecuba takes her revenge on Polymestor, the Thracian king who murdered her youngest son Polydorus for his gold: with the captive Trojan women she falls upon him and blinds him, a scene told in Euripides' Hecuba and in Ovid's Metamorphoses.
